newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes higher, boosted by crop data.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes higher, boosted by crop data.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed slightly higher, boosted primarily by bullish crop data issued by Statistics Canada, floor traders said.
A higher close in CBOT soybeans was also supportive.
Statistics Canada estimated Canadian canola production at 4.979 million tonnes, down from a previous projection, issued in late August, of 5.337 million.
"It is going to be tight (on stocks) and quality may also suffer with the harvest delays," one WCE oilseed trader said.
Delays have been most severe in Alberta and northern Saskatchewan, traders said.
Western barley futures closed lower, depressed mainly by continued concern that wet weather in Alberta will lead to more Alberta barley being graded feed quality.
"There is going to be more feed grain because of the quality problems. It has been wet (in Alberta) the last three weeks," one WCE feedgrain trader said.
Nov western barley closed $0.80 lower at $145.80.
Dec feed wheat finished up $0.40 at $172.00, October oats $3.40 up at $134.00, October flax gained $0.50 to $401.50 and December feed peas ended $0.50 higher at $205.00.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except for feed peas and oats which are in U.S. dollars).
